nodes.question: What are the best alternatives to combat environmental deterioration suggested in the study?
nodes.answer: The best alternatives are renewable energy, information & communication technology (ICT), and circular economy.
nodes.paragraph: The key challenges and best alternatives to environmental sustainability: a comprehensive study Syed Ale Raza Shah1 , Naila Abbas1, Luminita Serbanescu2, Rong Niu3 & Abdelmohsen A. Nassani4 In the modern world, the globe has been trapped by severe challenges, and an abrupt increase in environmental deterioration (ED) is one of these. The practitioners have recently tried to suggest several green initiatives to combat rising environmental concerns, but the problem remains intact. Most economies have priorities to meet their socio-economic target, and practitioners are unaware of true challenges and best alternatives. This study makes an effort to introduce the true challenges (income, urbanization, and natural resources) and best alternative (renewable energy, information & communication technology (ICT), and circular economy) for carbon footprint in the top 28 waste re- cycled economies (WRE) throughout 2000 2021. In order to obtain robust outcomes, the present study uses the most reliable estimators, and the Q-GMM is the most prominent. The outcomes describe a positive role of income, urbanization, and natural resources in carbon footprint.

nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What is one advantage of using essential oils (EOs) as an alternative to chemical herbicides?
nodes.answer: One advantage of using essential oils is that they cause no constraint on the environment due to their high volatility and biodegradability.
nodes.paragraph: email: sofiene.benkaab@uliege.be OPEN Scientific Reports www.nature.com/scientificreports by multisite actions in plant cells, which could slow the resistance of weeds to weed killers. Another advantage of EOs is that they cause no constraint on the environment due to their high volatility and biodegradability. Moreover, EOs have shown promising herbicidal activity. Considering these factors, they constitute a good alternative to chemical herbicides6 8. The phytotoxic effect of EOs on plants has been widely reported for the last 20 years. Numerous studies have shown this effect through the inhibition of seed germination and seedling growth9 17. For example, it has been shown that Rosmarinus officinalis EO, at lower concentrations, slows down the seedling growth of Trifolium incarnatum , Silybum marianum , and Phalaris minor , but at 5 mM, it completely inhibits seed germination11. This is similar to the finding 12, who reported that Thymbra capitata EO inhibited the germination and seedling growth of Erigeron canadensis L ., Sonchus oleraceus (L.) L., and Chenopodium album L . at 0.125 L/ml. In addition, several studies have described the site(s) of action of EOs18 21.
